truth: Cyrodiil is the Empire's heart: a broad basin of farmland round a great lake, ringed by mountains on three sides and opening to the sea and swamp in the south. Its people descend from slaves who overthrew the Ayleid elves, and the elves' white ruins still riddle the ground under every county. Roads radiate from the Imperial City on its lake island to nine walled cities, each with a chapel to one of the Nine and halls of the great guilds. The Oblivion Crisis has just ended: Kvatch lies burned, gate scars smoke in the hills, the throne is empty and the Elder Council, the guilds and the counts all reach for the power that is left.

jerall_mountains.truth: The Jerall Mountains form the cold northern rim where Cyrodiil meets Skyrim. Bruma is half Nord in blood and timber-and-stone building, a snow-roofed city guarding the only good pass, its Great Chapel of Talos raising the tallest spire in the county. Above it the Blades' cliff fortress of Cloud Ruler Temple watches the road, and to the west the dead Reman citadel of Sancre Tor broods on its peak. Life turns on herding, silver mining, pass trade and smuggling. The mountains hold more caves and old Imperial family crypts than any county, and the cold keeps the dead in them restless.

colovian_highlands.truth: The Colovian Highlands are a proud, dry upland of sheep downs, horse paddocks and broken limestone valleys running west to the High Rock and Hammerfell borders. Chorrol grew round a giant oak at the head of the Black Road and serves as the highland's market and the Fighters Guild's provincial seat. The people are plain-spoken Colovians who distrust the capital's ornate politics. Its karst caves hide warring goblin tribes, bandits and closed hill villages with secrets of their own, while the stone keeps of a Second Era war stand on every ridge.

heartlands.truth: The Heartlands are the lake country round the capital. The Imperial City stands on its central island, a wheel of six walled wards around the Ayleids' White-Gold Tower, reached by one monumental bridge. Around the shore run the Red Ring Road, rich grain farms, fishing villages and the first coaching inns of every highway. Wealth and power flow through here, and so does every rumour in Tamriel. Under the city run the sewers and pre-Imperial vaults; under the ploughed fields lie Ayleid ruins. The Elder Council's quarrels, the Arena's crowds and the Waterfront's thieves make this the busiest and most watched county.

great_forest.truth: The Great Forest is the old oak and beech woodland west and north-west of Lake Rumare, the densest ground for ancient ruins in Cyrodiil with more caves and Ayleid sites per mile than any other county. Few people live under its boughs, and those who do are loggers, charcoal-burners, priory monks and hunters who keep close to the roads. Minotaurs and wild beasts roam the deep glades, necromancers fortify the elven vaults, and roadside Daedric statues draw secret cultists. It is Cyrodiil's wild middle: golden-green by day, avoided at night, full of things the capital would rather forget.

nibenay_basin.truth: The Nibenay Basin is the fertile eastern valley between the Niben and the Valus Mountains, where Nibenese tattoo-art, silk and spice markets, and mystic orders meet Dunmer settlers from across the border passes. Cheydinhal straddles the Corbolo River under willow trees, with a Dunmer count in its castle and the Dark Brotherhood's sanctuary hidden beneath an abandoned house. Farms and orchards fill the plain, the Knights of the Thorn play at chivalry, and border keeps watch the Morrowind road while surviving Mythic Dawn cells lurk in the Lake Arrius caverns.

west_weald.truth: The West Weald is warm, sheltered vineyard country south-west of the Great Forest, straddling the Gold Road between the capital and the Abecean coast. Skingrad sits on its limestone hill between two sheer castle bridges, its vintner houses locked in a generational feud over whose cellar presses the finest vintage. Count Hassildor is almost never seen by daylight, and the townsfolk prefer not to ask why. Ayleid vaults—Miscarcand chief among them—lie under the vines, and the Priory of the Nine stands in the southern hills. It is golden and wealthy, with cold things in its cellars.

gold_coast.truth: The Gold Coast is Cyrodiil's western shore on the Abecean Sea and the dry hills behind it. Anvil is a bright harbour of white stone walls and blue roofs, its fleet and merchant houses rich on western sea trade. Up the Gold Road, Kvatch stood on its commanding hill until a Great Gate opened beneath it in the Oblivion Crisis: the city burned and its survivors camp below the walls while rebuilding begins. Between them run the longest leg of the Gold Road, smugglers' sea-caves, wreckers, a haunted manor and vampire lairs that prey on lonely travellers.

nibenay_valley.truth: The Nibenay Valley is the flat, wet and poor river country of the Lower Niben. Bravil is a crowded city of weathered plank houses built over mud canals and timber stilts beside the river, the poorest of the nine seats and the northern funnel for skooma smuggled up from Elsweyr. Its people trust luck more than the Watch and rub the statue of their Lucky Old Lady in the square for coin. The valley's riverbank caves and drowned Ayleid ruins shelter smugglers, necromancers and the sealed crypt where the Dark Brotherhood keeps its Night Mother.

blackwood.truth: Blackwood is hot, steaming swamp-forest where the Lower Niben meets Topal Bay on Cyrodiil's southern border with Black Marsh and Elsweyr. Leyawiin is a walled Imperial river-mouth city with Argonian and Khajiit shanties crowded outside its painted streets, and the home of the Blackwood Company, a mercenary outfit that has grown rich undercutting the Fighters Guild. Rumour says the company's men drink sap stolen from a marsh tree. Ayleid ruins sink into the peat, vampire covens and necromancers hide in the mangroves, and the border forts face an assertive Black Marsh.
